commands.about: Manage Affinidi Agent Gateway

Authenticate and save a named gateway connection.

Opens a browser for the gateway's passkey or SSO login and captures the token. Use --pat for a personal access token, or --paste, --token-stdin, or FABRIC_TOKEN for a session token. Piped standard input is read as the token.

The token is checked with the gateway before anything is saved. The connection is saved under --connection (or `default`) and becomes current; logging in again under the same name replaces it.

See docs/AUTHENTICATION.md for details.

Examples: Sign in through the browser and save the connection as "default": fabric agent-gateway login --host https://gateway.example.com

Save another connection, named "production": fabric agent-gateway --connection production login \ --host https://gateway.example.com

Sign in with a personal access token, prompted for without echo: fabric agent-gateway login --host https://gateway.example.com --pat

Sign in with a personal access token from a script: printf '%s' "$PAT" | fabric agent-gateway login \ --host https://gateway.example.com --pat --token-stdin

commands.about:
Preview which tools a set of MCP tool gates would allow or deny.

The gates come from a saved surface's own `target.mcp_tool_gating` (not its variants or transit points) or from --gates-file. Nothing is saved.

Pin what you know about the caller with --condition; other conditions are tried both ways (at most 3). A missing or disabled condition policy keeps a block gate on and an allow gate off, which the preview can't detect.

See docs/SURFACES.md for pattern rules and details.
commands.after_help:
Examples: Check the gates a surface has saved, named by its name or ID: fabric agent-gateway surfaces tool-gate-preview my-agent \ --tool delete_user,get_user

Check gates that are not saved yet, from a file: fabric agent-gateway surfaces tool-gate-preview --gates-file gates.json \ --tool delete_user

Say what you know about the caller (an admin who is not a contractor): fabric agent-gateway surfaces tool-gate-preview my-agent \ --tool delete_user --condition admins=met --condition contractors=unmet

Reading the result: RESULT is ALLOW or DENY. DECIDED BY is the gate that decided, or the default when no gate matched. A tool gets one row per combination of conditions, named in a CONDITION column, only when its answer or deciding gate depends on them. Otherwise each tool gets a single row and the CONDITION column is left out.
